question: The 5α reductase inhibitor that has been found to be effective both in benign prostatic hypertrophy and male pattern baldness is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "5α reductase inhibitor" -> "reduces dihydrotestosterone levels" -> "effective in treating benign prostatic hypertrophy" -> "also effective in male pattern baldness" -> "Finasteride" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Finasteride" -> "inhibits 5α reductase" -> "lowers DHT" -> "improves urinary symptoms in BPH" -> "promotes hair regrowth in male pattern baldness" -> 90%
CHAIN: "5α reductase inhibitors" -> "commonly used for BPH" -> "Finasteride is one of them" -> "also indicated for male pattern baldness" -> "other options do not have this dual indication" -> 85%
analysis: Finasteride is a well-established 5α reductase inhibitor that effectively lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT) levels. It is clinically proven to treat both benign prostatic hypertrophy (BPH) by alleviating urinary symptoms and male pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia) by promoting hair regrowth. The other options listed do not share this dual indication: Flutamide is an anti-androgen primarily used for prostate cancer, Prazosin is an alpha-1 blocker used for hypertension and BPH, and Minoxidil is a topical treatment for hair loss but not a 5α reductase inhibitor. Therefore, based on established medical knowledge and consensus, Finasteride is the correct answer.
